scope: Read-only audit of dependencies, startup, browser downloads, running app processes and local disk usage. No application changes, dependency installations, process stops or data deletions.

findings.title: Exclude browser-only dependencies from the Docker runtime
findings.evidence: npm prune --omit=dev retains MapLibre, React and React DOM, although the server imports none of these and Vite already bundles the frontend. The installed package-lock dependency closures contain 27 client-exclusive packages totaling 48,544,743 file bytes, after excluding shared server dependencies and nested node_modules from individual sizes.
findings.proposal: Move maplibre-gl, react and react-dom to devDependencies, update the lockfile, and let the existing production prune omit their exclusive dependencies. Keep polyclip-ts in runtime dependencies because src/boundary.ts imports it on the server.
findings.expectedSaving: Approximately 48.5 MB of unpacked runtime files on this installation; actual compressed image-layer savings require a Docker build measurement.
findings.validationNeeded: Build the image and verify server startup, drawn-boundary search validation and static frontend loading.

findings.title: Serve precompressed browser scripts and styles
findings.evidence: GET with Accept-Encoding: br, gzip returned uncompressed JavaScript with Content-Length 1064702 and no Content-Encoding. Map and worker scripts together contain 1,572,667 raw bytes. Compressing those exact built files locally produced 430,962 gzip bytes or 352,764 Brotli bytes.
findings.proposal: Generate .br/.gz siblings for text assets during the build using node:zlib and enable the existing @fastify/static preCompressed option. No additional runtime package is required. Avoid recompressing WOFF2 files.
findings.expectedSaving: About 1.22 MB / 78% of these two scripts' cold-transfer bytes with Brotli. This is a byte reduction, not a measured load-time or JavaScript parse-time improvement; local loopback makes timing impact smaller than hosted delivery.
findings.additionalEvidence: The catalog response is 735,008 uncompressed bytes, versus 241,695 gzip or 137,567 Brotli bytes in an offline compression experiment. Catalog compression would need a separate API response strategy.
findings.validationNeeded: Verify compressed and fallback HTTP responses, Content-Encoding, Vary: Accept-Encoding, and unchanged decoded content.

findings.title: Avoid dependency reinstall after a manual npm ci
findings.evidence: Startup trusts a custom node_modules/.alpine-lock stamp written only by this launcher. A manual npm ci recreates node_modules without this stamp, so the next npm start invokes npm ci again even when the dependency tree is current.
findings.proposal: Record the fingerprint after successful package installation, or validate npm's installed metadata against the project lockfile before deciding to reinstall. Continue detecting actual lockfile changes or missing dependencies.
findings.expectedSaving: One complete redundant installation after manual npm ci; download savings depend on the npm cache. The installed tree currently occupies about 135 MiB on disk.
findings.validationNeeded: Check fresh installation, manual npm ci followed by npm start, lockfile changes and missing required files.

findings.title: Reduce container healthcheck frequency
findings.evidence: The healthcheck launches a fresh Node process and HTTP request every 10 seconds: 8,640 launches per day of continuous container operation. docker ps returned no running containers during this audit, so this is configured overhead rather than current native-app overhead.
findings.proposal: Use a 30-60 second interval if slower unhealthy-state detection is acceptable. Retain readiness checks.
findings.expectedSaving: At 60 seconds, 7,200 fewer Node process launches per day when containerized; CPU and energy savings were not measured.

findings.title: Check build-output existence without reading file contents
findings.evidence: The exists helper uses readFile, including for every cached build output. Current outputs total roughly 2.43 MB across 57 files.
findings.proposal: Use filesystem stat/access for output existence; keep content hashing for actual build inputs.
findings.expectedSaving: A few MB of unnecessary file reads on native startup; low priority.

diskOnlyOpportunities.maintainerCacheNote: Not used by the running app. Files in progressive-feasibility/shared-sources remain referenced by active preparation manifests; deleting them would cause future preparation to download again.
diskOnlyOpportunities.retainedJobNote: Includes a large legacy result. History is intentionally retained until manual deletion; do not automatically clean it up. No database was opened for this audit.
diskOnlyOpportunities.note: Review backup/release/intermediate retention before removal. These are disk savings, not demonstrated runtime speedups. No files were deleted.

alreadyEfficient: All six direct application dependencies have an actual use; browser-only runtime packaging is the removable excess, not the frontend functionality.

One native app server was observed, with no active jobs and no running Docker containers. A later ps snapshot reported 30,752 KiB RSS and 0.0% CPU; this is a point-in-time observation, not a sustained benchmark.
Map worker count is already one, search workers run only during jobs, and the search memory watchdog is cleared afterward.
Idle or hidden browser job polling backs off to 15 seconds; active visible job polling uses one second.
The installed pinned catalog is reused; prepared sections are downloaded on demand. Runtime section assets total 138,934,836 bytes.
Browser asset inventory showed only the two Latin UI font subsets loading; Latin Extended subsets did not load in the inspected view.

Static assets have ETags and return 304 Not Modified for a matching validator. max-age=0 causes revalidation, not necessarily a complete redownload. Long immutable caching on fingerprinted /assets files is a minor optional improvement; keep index.html revalidated.
The public basemap has four terrain sources with differing tileSize values used by four relief layers. They are intentional visual passes; duplicated source URLs alone do not justify removing them.
limitations: Dedicated Chrome performance trace tools were unavailable and the in-app browser's read-only evaluator did not expose performance entries. No Core Web Vitals, long-task, GPU or request-duration claims are made.
Compression numbers are offline experiments on current files, not deployed compression measurements.
A concurrent build changed fingerprinted filenames during the audit. Byte sizes and source behavior were inspected after that build; no running server was restarted.
No app tests were run because this audit changed no application code.

changes: Moved React, React DOM and MapLibre to build-only dependencies, retaining polyclip-ts for server boundary validation.
Generated Brotli (quality 9) and gzip siblings for text build assets using Node built-ins, and enabled static compression negotiation.
Cached fingerprinted assets immutably for one year while preserving fresh HTML and API metadata.
Added a postinstall dependency fingerprint so manual npm ci is reused by npm start.
Used stat metadata for cached build-output existence checks.
Changed container healthchecks to 60 seconds with five-second startup checks.
Included existing public font license in container build inputs.

validation.staticNegotiation: passed Brotli/gzip/identity decoding, cache policy, missing assets and fresh API/HTML
validation.appFlows: 19 passed; localhost fixture test rerun with network access after sandbox timeout
validation.manualInstall: Actual offline npm ci in temporary native checkout recorded its stamp; ensureDependencies did not reinstall
validation.container: Built and ran as non-root with temporary fixture and no live volume; verified frontend dependency absence, drawn-boundary search, completed hike, GPX and font license
validation.compose: Configuration validated on Docker Compose v5.1.2

implementation.dataPolicy: Caches, backups, downloaded trail sections and saved-job files were not deleted. The idle native server was gracefully restarted; all 15 saved jobs retained their IDs and statuses.
notes: Brotli quality 9 keeps build cost modest; achieved transfer reduction is about 75%, below the audit experiment with default quality 11.
Catalog API compression was an additional measurement, not one of the selected implementation changes; API responses retain no-store.
Existing concurrent app edits were preserved. Temporary task worktree archived and verification container automatically removed.
